subject: english-language
title: How We Speak
welcome_lead: Speech is full of clues about who we are and where we're.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on standard English and dialects.
final_note: You can now tell standard English from dialect features.

concepts.def: Words and grammar of a region.

walkthroughs.body_html: Standard English is the form used in news, exams and most writing. It's not 'correct' speech — just shared.
An accent is how words sound. A dialect is the words and grammar themselves ('I were' instead of 'I was').
Slang is informal and often new ('peng', 'banger'). Colloquial covers everyday phrasing. Both are valid in casual contexts.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between transitive and intransitive verbs?
options: Transitive verbs are action verbs and intransitive are linking verbs.
Transitive verbs take a direct object ('she ate the cake'); intransitive verbs don't ('she slept'). Some verbs are both depending on use ('she ran' / 'she ran the company').
Transitive verbs end in -ed and intransitive in -ing.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
